`fhi-innvandrere` has one model, 32,720 rows and no published
series. Four parties had each built a different partial proxy
for the question this field looks like it answers, and three
were wrong the same day (urb-agents #1344).

🔴 AND THIS NUMBER CAN CHANGE FOR TWO REASONS THAT LOOK
IDENTICAL. Either a model genuinely shipped, or the lineage it
is computed from was CORRECTED. A consumer reading it twice
cannot tell an honest value change from an accuracy fix: on
2026-09-21 the demo consumer read it morning and evening, got
9 and 1, and had no way to know which it was seeing
(urb-agents #1348).

🔵 `lineage` is generated from the dbt manifest and committed,
so it can be stale — 103 edges were missing that day, some for
weeks. `check-lineage-is-current.sh` now fails CI on drift, so
the accuracy kind of change should stop happening. It cannot
be detected retroactively in a value you already read.

served_as.description:
The `api_v1` relations a consumer can actually reach this source
through, as a Postgres `text[]`. **Empty means nothing published
depends on it** — that is the gap, and it is the one question
`downstream_model_count` cannot answer.

Filter for the gap with `?served_as=eq.{}`, or for a specific
surface with `?served_as=cs.{indicator_summary}`.

🔵 NOT A PLAIN LINEAGE JOIN, DELIBERATELY. A relation derived
from `fact_kommune_indicators` is only claimed when the source
actually has rows in that fact.

The case that forced that design: `ssb-06913` fed the fact and
so reached four published relations on paper while contributing
ZERO rows to them — its `kommune_nr` regex never matched, so
783,104 rows were discarded downstream. A structural boolean
would have called it served and become the fifth wrong proxy.
It was fixed the same day (urb-agents #1345) and now reports
those four relations, which is the column working rather than
the example expiring.

⚠️ THE CATALOGUE RELATIONS ARE EXCLUDED. `meta_sources`,
`meta_endpoints` and `meta_dimensions` hold a row for every
source by construction, so naming them would be the same value
on every row. They describe a source; they do not serve it.

🔴 IT DOES NOT ASSERT THAT ANY NAMED RELATION CONTAINS ROWS.
For a relation derived from the fact, the source is checked to
have rows there. For every other relation the claim is
LINEAGE ONLY — what the source WOULD serve if it had data.

⚠️ THE CASE THAT PROVES IT: `redcross-branches` has
`total_runs` 0 and has never ingested, and it still lists five
relations, three of which hold zero rows. A source that has
never run looks served.

🔵 THE COMPANION CHECK IS ON THIS SAME ROW. Read `served_as`
with `total_runs` and `latest_row_count`: lineage says what
could arrive, those say whether anything did.

⚠️ AN EARLIER VERSION OF THIS PARAGRAPH SAID THE SAME THING AND
DID NOT WORK. It read "for non-fact relations this is
reachability, not volume", naming `brreg_enhet` and
`dim_kommune` — relations that are never empty, so the warning
was abstract. ops-dev read it and built a gate on the field
within the hour (urb-agents #1346). A caveat that names no
failing case is a caveat nobody applies.

🔵 Excluding never-ingested sources outright was considered and
rejected: it would collapse "has never run" into "is not
modelled", losing the distinction between `redcross-branches`
(five relations waiting for data) and the sources deferred in
BACKLOG (no relation at all). Say the word if that trade is
wrong.

🔵 Derived from the same artefact the CI gate reads, so the two
cannot drift: `check-every-source-is-served.sh` and this column
both resolve the source against the generated `api_v1` relation
list.

⚠️ THE GATE AND THIS COLUMN CAN DISAGREE, AND THAT IS CORRECT.
The gate is static and cannot see a source that is wired up and
delivers nothing, so it will report fewer gaps than this column
does. The gate answers "is it wired"; this answers "does it
arrive". Neither count is written here on purpose — a number in
a published description goes stale silently, which is most of
why this column had to be written at all.

indicator_missing_kommuner.description:
🔴 A ROW HERE IS NOT EVIDENCE OF LOW NEED. For `fhi-*` sources it is
usually FHI's disclosure suppression: it hides numbers based on fewer
than ~6 cases, and hides a whole series when more than 20% of it is
hidden, "for ikke å skape et skjevt inntrykk av situasjonen i
kommunen" — to avoid a skewed impression of that kommune.

⚠️ Measured: 105 kommuner are missing from 10+ `fhi-*` series, median
population 1,452, monotonic in population, and EVERY kommune is absent
from at least three. Treating absence as zero in a ranked index
inverts the signal for the smallest kommuner (urb-agents #1379). See
`indicator_summary.kommuners_with_null`.

One row per (source_id, contents_code, kommune_nr) for every
active kommune that has *no* non-NULL value at the indicator's
latest_year. The "coverage gap" sidebar on the data explorer
detail page; equivalent to the listMissingKommuner() inline query.

PostgREST consumers filter via
?source_id=eq.X&contents_code=eq.Y. Membership semantics: a
kommune is considered "missing" if it either has no row at
latest_year, or has a row with value IS NULL. Status markers (':',
'X') do not count as a value.

The full table is the cross-product of every indicator with every
active kommune that lacks data. Most cells are present, so the
unfiltered row count is the per-indicator gap-list aggregated
across all indicators.

kommune_nr.description:
4-digit zero-padded kommune code. FK to dim_kommune; only
active kommuner with no value at latest_year are listed.

rowFilter.coverage_gap_barnefattigdom.ko.name: kommune_nr
rowFilter.coverage_gap_barnefattigdom.ko.description:
4-digit zero-padded kommune code. FK to dim_kommune; only
active kommuner are included. Unique within this view.

rowFilter.coverage_gap_barnefattigdom.fy.name: fylke_name
rowFilter.coverage_gap_barnefattigdom.fy.description:
Joined from fact_kommune_indicators (originally from
dim_fylke). NULL for kommuner whose fylke_nr isn't in
dim_fylke (rare — Svalbard 21xx).

rowFilter.coverage_gap_barnefattigdom.ye.name: year
rowFilter.coverage_gap_barnefattigdom.ye.description:
The latest year for ssb-08764/EUskala60. Same value across all
rows; carried on each row so the consumer reads it without a
separate query.

rowFilter.coverage_gap_barnefattigdom.va.name: value_pct
rowFilter.coverage_gap_barnefattigdom.va.description:
EU-skala 60 % share — the percent of children under 18 in
low-income households (defined as < 60 % of national median
equivalised income). NULL when upstream suppressed the cell.

rowFilter.coverage_gap_barnefattigdom.pe.name: personer
rowFilter.coverage_gap_barnefattigdom.pe.description:
DENOMINATOR, NOT A COUNT OF POOR CHILDREN. Every person under
18 in the kommune that year — SSB 08764 ContentsCode
'Personer', whose own metadata reads "Persons under 18 years
of age", unit persons.

The number of children in low-income households is
personer * value_pct / 100. It is not published as a column;
derive it.

This description said "number of children under 18 in
low-income households" until 2026-09-19, which is false by
roughly ninefold and about child poverty. A consumer building
on the published API summed the column, got 1,097,107 against
a national under-18 population of about 1.1 million, and
caught it (urb-agents #1250, #1251). Derived correctly the
same sum is 124,670, near the ~11 % national rate.

Nothing in the data contradicted the wrong reading: the
column is plausible, non-null and internally consistent, and
only summing it and recognising the total gives it away. The
view description two entries above was right the whole time,
so the contract disagreed with itself.

NULL when upstream suppressed the cell.

rowFilter.coverage_gap_barnefattigdom.ba.name: barn_i_lavinntekt
rowFilter.coverage_gap_barnefattigdom.ba.description:
Children under 18 in low-income households — the number most
consumers come here for. DERIVED as
personer * value_pct / 100, rounded.

SSB does not publish this. Table 08764 carries the total and
the shares only, so every consumer has to compute it, and one
got it wrong because the `personer` description claimed to be
this column already (urb-agents #1250, #1251). Added on
Terje's authorisation rather than renaming `personer`, so the
consumer that found the defect keeps working.

ESTIMATE, NOT A COUNT. value_pct is published to one decimal,
so the true value lies within ±0.05 % of personer: about ±65
children for Oslo, ±4 for a kommune of 7 000. Do not present
it as SSB's own figure.

NULL when either input was suppressed upstream.

rowFilter.kommune_local_chapters.kommune.name: kommune_nr
rowFilter.kommune_local_chapters.kommune.description:
🔴 WHERE THE CHAPTER IS REGISTERED, NOT WHERE IT WORKS. This
description said "where the local chapter operates" until
2026-09-20 and that was a stronger claim than the data
supports: the value is a dim_postnummer lookup on the
chapter's POSTAL ADDRESS (see supply__redcross_branches).

⚠️ So a chapter serving three neighbouring kommuner appears in
one of them, and a chapter with a PO box in the next kommune
appears in the wrong one. A consumer asking "is Røde Kors
here?" gets "is Røde Kors registered here?" — which is the
same limitation as searching the Enhetsregisteret by name, and
this relation does not remove it (urb-agents #1289).

Declared service areas are not modelled for Red Cross at all.
`marts.chapter_kommune_coverage` holds one row per
(regional chapter, kommune), but its rows are INFERRED from
where the regional chapter's local children are registered —
so it inherits this same defect rather than fixing it, and it
is not published to api_v1.

FK to dim_kommune, the primary filter dimension for this view.
Chapters with NULL kommune_nr are excluded (this isn't "local
chapters in a kommune" if there's no kommune).

⚠️ The relationships test is `warn`-severity because
Longyearbyen Røde Kors is a real chapter whose Svalbard code
is not in dim_kommune — SSB Klass 131 contains no 21xx code.
So this relation is built to publish a Svalbard row that no
dimension can describe. See urb-agents #700.

rowFilter.kommune_local_chapters.chapter.name: chapter_id
rowFilter.kommune_local_chapters.chapter.description:
Composite slug for the local chapter (e.g.
'redcross-oslo-grunerløkka'). Repeats across rows when the
chapter offers multiple service categories.

rowFilter.kommune_local_chapters.name.name: name
rowFilter.kommune_local_chapters.name.description: Display name for the local chapter.

rowFilter.kommune_local_chapters.ngo_org.name: ngo_orgnr
rowFilter.kommune_local_chapters.ngo_org.description: 9-digit Brreg organisasjonsnummer of the NGO that owns the chapter.

rowFilter.kommune_local_chapters.ngo_bra.name: ngo_brand_name
rowFilter.kommune_local_chapters.ngo_bra.description:
Joined from dim_ngo (brand name when distinct from legal
name). NULL when the NGO doesn't use a brand alias.

rowFilter.kommune_local_chapters.service.name: service_category_code
rowFilter.kommune_local_chapters.service.description:
ICNPO-derived service category code for one of the activities
this chapter offers. Combined with chapter_id forms the
natural key of this view (rows are unique on
(chapter_id, service_category_code)).

rowFilter.kommune_local_chapters.service.name: service_category_label_no
rowFilter.kommune_local_chapters.service.description:
Human-readable Norwegian label for service_category_code,
joined from ref_atlas_service_category.

rowFilter.kommune_local_chapters.sort_or.name: sort_order
rowFilter.kommune_local_chapters.sort_or.description:
Display order from ref_atlas_service_category. Used by the UI
to render service categories in a consistent sequence; carry
on the row so consumers can sort without a separate query.

rowFilter.meta_dimensions.source_id.name: source_id
rowFilter.meta_dimensions.source_id.description:
Source the dimension belongs to. Joins to
`mart_meta_sources.source_id` and `_sources_manifest.source_id`.

rowFilter.meta_dimensions.code.name: code
rowFilter.meta_dimensions.code.description:
Upstream's own dimension code (e.g. `Region`, `Tid`,
`ContentsCode` for SSB; `GEO`, `AAR`, `KJONN`, `MEASURE_TYPE`
for FHI). Verbatim from the source's API/export — not
translated to canonical Atlas vocabulary.

rowFilter.meta_dimensions.meaning.name: meaning
rowFilter.meta_dimensions.meaning.description:
Short human-readable description of what the dimension
represents. Hand-authored editorial content from each source's
`manifest.yml` `dimensions:` block.

rowFilter.meta_dimensions.value_format.name: value_format
rowFilter.meta_dimensions.value_format.description:
Encoding of values within the dimension (e.g. "4-digit year as
text", "1- to 6-character numeric code"). Empty string when no
specific format applies.

rowFilter.meta_dimensions.notes.name: notes
rowFilter.meta_dimensions.notes.description:
Editorial notes — code-list size, semantic gotchas, downstream
filtering decisions. Empty string when no notes apply.

rowFilter.ngo_overview.orgnr.name: orgnr
rowFilter.ngo_overview.orgnr.description: 9-digit Brreg organisasjonsnummer. Natural key for this view.

rowFilter.ngo_overview.chapter_count.name: chapter_count
rowFilter.ngo_overview.chapter_count.description: Total count of chapters for this NGO across all levels (active + inactive).

rowFilter.ngo_overview.regional_count.name: regional_count
rowFilter.ngo_overview.regional_count.description: Count of chapters at chapter_level = 'regional' (e.g. Red Cross distrikt).

rowFilter.ngo_overview.local_count.name: local_count
rowFilter.ngo_overview.local_count.description: Count of chapters at chapter_level = 'local' (the kommune-bound branches).

rowFilter.ngo_overview.activity_count.name: activity_count
rowFilter.ngo_overview.activity_count.description:
Count of distinct activities offered by this NGO (rows in
dim_activity for this orgnr).

rowFilter.ngo_overview.kommune_count.name: kommune_count
rowFilter.ngo_overview.kommune_count.description:
Count of distinct kommuner with at least one active local
chapter for this NGO. The "footprint" metric for coverage-gap
questions.

rowFilter.brreg_enhet.organisasjonsnumme.name: organisasjonsnummer
rowFilter.brreg_enhet.organisasjonsnumme.description: Nine-digit Norwegian organisation number. Text, never a number — leading zeros are significant. Stable for the life of the organisation, and the join key for organisational data from any Norwegian source.

rowFilter.brreg_enhet.navn.name: navn
rowFilter.brreg_enhet.navn.description: Registered name, verbatim from Brreg. For an enkeltpersonforetak (organisasjonsform ENK) this is very often the proprietor's own personal name, because that is how the register records them.

rowFilter.brreg_enhet.organisasjonsform_.name: organisasjonsform_kode
rowFilter.brreg_enhet.organisasjonsform_.description: Legal form code — AS (aksjeselskap), ENK (enkeltpersonforetak), FLI (forening/lag/innretning), STI (stiftelse) and others. The usual filter for separating companies from associations, or for excluding sole proprietorships.

rowFilter.brreg_enhet.organisasjonsform_.name: organisasjonsform_beskrivelse
rowFilter.brreg_enhet.organisasjonsform_.description: Human-readable Norwegian label for organisasjonsform_kode, as Brreg publishes it.

rowFilter.brreg_enhet.naeringskode1_kode.name: naeringskode1_kode
rowFilter.brreg_enhet.naeringskode1_kode.description: Primary NACE industry code (SN2007), e.g. 94.992. Null for roughly 2% of the register.

rowFilter.brreg_enhet.kommune_nr.name: kommune_nr
rowFilter.brreg_enhet.kommune_nr.description: Kommune code of the registered business address. For an enkeltpersonforetak the registered business address is commonly the proprietor's home address. Null where no business address is registered (~6%). Some codes are historical or pseudo-regions and will not resolve against a current kommune list.

rowFilter.brreg_enhet.antall_ansatte.name: antall_ansatte
rowFilter.brreg_enhet.antall_ansatte.description: Registered employee count. NULL MEANS "NOT REPORTED", NOT ZERO — the field is present on only ~4% of records. Use har_registrert_antall_ansatte to distinguish the two; reading NULL as 0 understates staffed organisations badly.

rowFilter.brreg_enhet.har_registrert_ant.name: har_registrert_antall_ansatte
rowFilter.brreg_enhet.har_registrert_ant.description: Whether Brreg holds a registered employee count at all. Present on 100% of records, and the only way to tell "zero employees" from "no figure reported".

rowFilter.brreg_enhet.konkurs.name: konkurs
rowFilter.brreg_enhet.konkurs.description: Whether the organisation is in bankruptcy proceedings. Straight from Brreg.

rowFilter.brreg_enhet.under_avvikling.name: under_avvikling
rowFilter.brreg_enhet.under_avvikling.description: Whether the organisation is being wound up voluntarily. Straight from Brreg.

rowFilter.brreg_enhet.under_tvangsavvikl.name: under_tvangsavvikling
rowFilter.brreg_enhet.under_tvangsavvikl.description: Whether the organisation is under compulsory winding-up or dissolution.

rowFilter.brreg_enhet.is_active.name: is_active
rowFilter.brreg_enhet.is_active.description: Convenience boolean — true when none of konkurs, under_avvikling or under_tvangsavvikling is set. Means "trading", not "exists": all three states are still registered organisations. Ignore this column if you want everything registered.

rowFilter.brreg_enhet.registrert_i_frivi.name: registrert_i_frivillighetsregisteret
rowFilter.brreg_enhet.registrert_i_frivi.description: Whether the organisation is in Frivillighetsregisteret, the voluntary-organisation register — true for roughly 72,800 records. This is what makes the Norwegian voluntary sector discoverable as a population rather than a curated list.

rowFilter.brreg_enhet.registrert_dato.name: registrert_dato
rowFilter.brreg_enhet.registrert_dato.description: Date the organisation was entered in Enhetsregisteret.

rowFilter.brreg_enhet.icnpo_nummer.name: icnpo_nummer
rowFilter.brreg_enhet.icnpo_nummer.description: Primary ICNPO code as the organisation classified itself in Frivillighetsregisteret, e.g. "9100". Null for organisations not in that register, and for members declaring none. Null does not mean "not voluntary" — use registrert_i_frivillighetsregisteret for that.

rowFilter.brreg_enhet.icnpo_kategori.name: icnpo_kategori
rowFilter.brreg_enhet.icnpo_kategori.description: Primary ICNPO category label paired with icnpo_nummer.

rowFilter.brreg_enhet.grasrotandel_delta.name: grasrotandel_deltar_i
rowFilter.brreg_enhet.grasrotandel_delta.description: Whether the organisation participates in Grasrotandelen, Norsk Tipping's grassroots funding scheme. Null for organisations not in Frivillighetsregisteret.

rowFilter.brreg_enhet.frivillig_innfoert.name: frivillig_innfoert_dato
rowFilter.brreg_enhet.frivillig_innfoert.description: Date of entry in Frivillighetsregisteret — distinct from registrert_dato, which is the Enhetsregisteret entry. Organisations often exist for years before registering as voluntary.

rowFilter.brreg_enhet.last_seen_at.name: last_seen_at
rowFilter.brreg_enhet.last_seen_at.description: When the INGEST last wrote this row into Atlas's raw layer, from either the bulk snapshot or a change-feed run. Tracks Atlas's load, not an upstream event. Read it together with reconciled_at — this is the ingest clock, that is the transform clock.

rowFilter.brreg_enhet.reconciled_at.name: reconciled_at
rowFilter.brreg_enhet.reconciled_at.description: When the TRANSFORM last reconciled this row into the served layer. 🔴 Read both clocks: the change feed polls every half hour and this reconciliation follows ten minutes behind it, so the data behind this endpoint can be older than what Atlas has already ingested. Without both, "current" means different things depending on which table you read — an install once sat 13.5 hours behind Brreg with every health check green. ⚠️ Only organisations that actually changed are re-stamped, so an old value means "nothing about this organisation has changed since then", not "this endpoint is stale".

rowFilter.brreg_enhet.doc.name: doc
rowFilter.brreg_enhet.doc.description: The complete upstream record as Brreg published it, with nothing dropped or renamed — including postal and business addresses, telephone, mobile, email, website, capital, institutional sector code, articles of association and historical names. Responses are large: a document averages ~1.7 kB, so select the typed columns instead unless you need a field this view does not surface.

rowFilter.bufdir_indicator_alias.source_.name: source_id
rowFilter.bufdir_indicator_alias.source_.description:
Source the alias applies to. Always `bufdir-barnefattigdom`
today; forward-looking column kept so other ZIP sources can
adopt the same convention without a schema migration.

rowFilter.bufdir_indicator_alias.histori.name: historical_id
rowFilter.bufdir_indicator_alias.histori.description:
Previous `indicator_api_id` from an earlier bufdir release —
the id consumers may have cached and now need to bridge to
the current canonical id. Same shape as
`indicators__bufdir_barnefattigdom.indicator_api_id`
(`bf_zip_ind_<N>`).

rowFilter.bufdir_indicator_alias.canonic.name: canonical_id
rowFilter.bufdir_indicator_alias.canonic.description:
Current `indicator_api_id`, or NULL when the historical
indicator was retired without a successor. NULL is meaningful:
consumers treat such rows as terminating series rather than
orphans.

rowFilter.bufdir_indicator_alias.note.name: note
rowFilter.bufdir_indicator_alias.note.description:
Editorial explanation of the renumbering event — why the
historical id maps to this canonical id, or why no successor
exists. One sentence; read by humans, not parsers.

rowFilter.indicator_latest_values.source.name: source_id
rowFilter.indicator_latest_values.source.description:
Atlas source identifier, e.g. 'ssb-08764'. Joins back to
fact_kommune_indicators.source_id.

rowFilter.indicator_latest_values.conten.name: contents_code
rowFilter.indicator_latest_values.conten.description:
Source-specific ContentsCode verbatim from upstream (e.g.
'EUskala60', 'Folkemengde'). Combined with source_id and
kommune_nr forms the natural key of this view.

rowFilter.indicator_latest_values.kommun.name: kommune_nr
rowFilter.indicator_latest_values.kommun.description:
4-digit zero-padded kommune code. FK to dim_kommune; only
active kommuner are included.

rowFilter.indicator_latest_values.fylke_.name: fylke_name
rowFilter.indicator_latest_values.fylke_.description:
Joined from fact_kommune_indicators (originally from
dim_fylke). NULL when the kommune's fylke_nr isn't present in
dim_fylke (rare — happens for codes like Svalbard 21xx).

rowFilter.indicator_latest_values.value.name: value
rowFilter.indicator_latest_values.value.description:
Numeric value at latest_year. Unit depends on (source_id,
contents_code) — see the source's README. NULL when upstream
suppressed the cell.

rowFilter.indicator_latest_values.status.name: status
rowFilter.indicator_latest_values.status.description:
SSB suppression marker (e.g. ':' for 'not available'). NULL
when value is present.

rowFilter.indicator_latest_values.year.name: year
rowFilter.indicator_latest_values.year.description:
The latest year for this (source_id, contents_code). Repeats
across all kommuner for a given indicator — kept on the row so
PostgREST consumers can read it without a separate join.

⚠️ For a windowed source this is the FIRST year of the window.
Render it with `window_years`, never alone.

rowFilter.indicator_latest_values.window.name: window_years
rowFilter.indicator_latest_values.window.description:
How many calendar years `year` covers, carried from
fact_kommune_indicators. 1 for an annual series. The span is
`year` to `year + window_years - 1` inclusive. See
`mart_indicator_summary.latest_year_window_years` for why this
is a column rather than prose.

rowFilter.kommune_ngo_summary.kommune_na.name: kommune_name
rowFilter.kommune_ngo_summary.kommune_na.description: Kommune name in bokmål, joined from dim_kommune.

rowFilter.kommune_ngo_summary.icnpo_numm.name: icnpo_nummer
rowFilter.kommune_ngo_summary.icnpo_numm.description:
ICNPO category number as Brreg assigns it. NULL where the
organisation carries no ICNPO classification.

rowFilter.kommune_ngo_summary.icnpo_kate.name: icnpo_kategori
rowFilter.kommune_ngo_summary.icnpo_kate.description:
ICNPO category label. NULL where the organisation carries no
ICNPO classification — those rows are counted, not dropped,
so a per-kommune total over this view stays correct.

rowFilter.kommune_ngo_summary.active_cou.name: active_count
rowFilter.kommune_ngo_summary.active_cou.description:
Count of organisations in this kommune and category that are
both is_active and registrert_i_frivillighetsregisteret.
Always >= 1; absent combinations mean zero.

rowFilter.meta_endpoints.table_name.name: table_name
rowFilter.meta_endpoints.table_name.description: Bare table/view name without schema qualification.

rowFilter.meta_endpoints.tags.name: tags
rowFilter.meta_endpoints.tags.description:
`text[]` carrying the layer tag (`layer:<schema>`) plus inherited
source tags via union semantics. Filter via PostgREST's
`?tags=cs.{...}` array-contains operator.

rowFilter.meta_endpoints.is_public_api.name: is_public_api
rowFilter.meta_endpoints.is_public_api.description:
`true` when `schema_name = 'api_v1'`. Lets clients distinguish
stable-contract endpoints from the broader `marts.*` / `raw.*`
surfaces that are queryable but not version-guaranteed.

rowFilter.meta_endpoints.table_type.name: table_type
rowFilter.meta_endpoints.table_type.description:
`BASE TABLE` for tables (most `marts.*`, all `raw.*`) and
`VIEW` for views (all `api_v1.*` wrappers).

⚠️ IN `api_v1` IT IS ALWAYS `VIEW` AND THEREFORE TELLS YOU
NOTHING ON ITS OWN. All 17 public relations are views over a
`marts.mart_*` relation; this column distinguishes them from
`marts.*` and `raw.*`, not from each other.

🔴 IT DOES NOT PREDICT WHETHER `Prefer: count=estimated` CAN BE
TRUSTED. Three cases, and the deciding property is whether the
aggregation happened BEFORE the planner saw it:

1. the mart is a TABLE — 14 of 17. Its rows were counted by
   ANALYZE when it was built, whatever its query did, so the
   estimate is accurate. `indicator_summary` aggregates heavily
   and estimates fine, because the aggregating happened at
   build time.
2. the mart is a PLAIN VIEW — `brreg_enhet`. Row count
   propagates from the base table. Accurate.
3. the mart is an AGGREGATING VIEW — `kommune_ngo_summary` and
   `kommune_ngo_totals`, and only these. The planner must guess
   how many groups a GROUP BY will produce, and measured on the
   live API 2026-09-20 it guessed badly:

       kommune_ngo_summary   exact 5 435   estimated 69 462   12.8x
       kommune_ngo_totals    exact   357   estimated  6 946   19.5x

⚠️ AND SEPARATELY, `estimated = 1` DOES NOT MEAN ONE ROW. It is
the planner's floor, so an EMPTY relation reports 1 — measured
on activity_catalog, distrikt_summary and kommune_local_chapters,
all of which hold zero rows and all of which are case 1. A
consumer asking "is there any data here?" cheaply gets yes.

✅ Use `Prefer: count=exact`. The largest published relation is
~72 000 rows and an exact count is cheap; the estimate saves
nothing worth being wrong about.

🔵 An earlier version of this description said the split was
tables versus views. There are no tables in api_v1, so that
rule was unusable — a consumer checking dim_kommune, a view
that estimates exactly, would have concluded the documentation
was wrong (urb-agents #1288).

rowFilter.dim_kommune.kommune_nr.name: kommune_nr
rowFilter.dim_kommune.kommune_nr.description:
4-digit zero-padded kommune code, SSB canonical form
('0301' = Oslo). The join key every other Atlas relation uses.

rowFilter.dim_kommune.kommune_name_alt.name: kommune_name_alt
rowFilter.dim_kommune.kommune_name_alt.description:
The alternative official name where SSB publishes one —
in practice the Sámi variant, split out of upstream's
"Name - Nama" string rather than left embedded in
kommune_name. NULL for most kommuner.

rowFilter.dim_kommune.fylke_nr.name: fylke_nr
rowFilter.dim_kommune.fylke_nr.description:
2-digit fylke code, derived from the first two digits of
kommune_nr per SSB's long-standing convention.

rowFilter.dim_kommune.fylke_name.name: fylke_name
rowFilter.dim_kommune.fylke_name.description:
Joined from dim_fylke. NULL where the fylke code is not in
dim_fylke — pseudo-regions and Svalbard (21xx) — rather than
dropping the kommune, so an unresolvable fylke costs a label
and not a row.

rowFilter.dim_kommune.is_active.name: is_active
rowFilter.dim_kommune.is_active.description:
True when the CODE is current — which is not the same as "this
is a municipality". 358 rows satisfy it: 357 kommuner plus the
9999 sentinel. Combine with is_sentinel.

⚠️ Sentinel codes such as 9999 'Uoppgitt' are present in this
dimension and reach api_v1 views unmarked — whether they
should be excluded or flagged is an open product question
(urb-agents #700), raised again by a consumer whose first
build reported 358 kommuner and carried a null-everything row
into a chart.

rowFilter.dim_kommune.valid_from.name: valid_from
rowFilter.dim_kommune.valid_from.description: Date the code became valid. NULL where upstream gives none.

rowFilter.dim_kommune.valid_to.name: valid_to
rowFilter.dim_kommune.valid_to.description: Date the code became inactive. NULL = still active.

rowFilter.dim_kommune.notes.name: notes
rowFilter.dim_kommune.notes.description:
Upstream's own note on the code, typically recording a merger
or reorganisation. NULL for most rows.

rowFilter.dim_kommune.is_sentinel.name: is_sentinel
rowFilter.dim_kommune.is_sentinel.description:
True for SSB's 9999 'Uoppgitt' bucket — a current code that is
not a municipality.

⚠️ is_active does NOT exclude it. `?is_active=eq.true` returns
358, not 357, and the extra row is this one (measured on the
live API, urb-agents #1265). For real municipalities filter
`?is_sentinel=is.false`.

🔵 THIS RELATION KEEPS THE ROW ON PURPOSE, AND IT IS NOW THE
ONLY PUBLISHED ONE THAT DOES. SSB's Klass 131 contains 9999,
and this dimension mirrors SSB's kommune list — dropping it
would mean Atlas's list no longer matches the source anyone
would reconcile against.

⚠️ As of 2026-09-21 the ANALYTICAL relations no longer carry
it: coverage_gap_barnefattigdom, indicator_latest_values,
indicator_missing_kommuner and kommune_ngo_summary exclude it,
and indicator_summary stopped counting it in its coverage
figures. Those are Atlas's own constructs and their grain is
"one municipality"; this one is a mirror. Terje's decision,
urb-agents #1301.

The unattributable value it represented is published in
`unattributed_totals`, not discarded.

rowFilter.kommune_ngo_totals.kommune_nam.name: kommune_name
rowFilter.kommune_ngo_totals.kommune_nam.description: Kommune name in bokmål, joined from dim_kommune.

rowFilter.kommune_ngo_totals.active_coun.name: active_count
rowFilter.kommune_ngo_totals.active_coun.description:
Total active voluntary organisations in this kommune, summed
across ICNPO categories. Always >= 1; a kommune with none has
no row.

rowFilter.kommune_befolkning_alder.kommu.name: kommune_name
rowFilter.kommune_befolkning_alder.kommu.description: Kommune name in bokmål, joined from dim_kommune.

rowFilter.kommune_befolkning_alder.fylke.name: fylke_nr
rowFilter.kommune_befolkning_alder.fylke.description: 2-digit fylke code, derived from kommune_nr in dim_kommune.

rowFilter.kommune_befolkning_alder.fylke.name: fylke_name
rowFilter.kommune_befolkning_alder.fylke.description: Joined from dim_fylke. NULL for kommune codes whose fylke has no row there — Svalbard-style 21xx codes. A LEFT join on purpose: an inner one would drop those kommuner from the denominator entirely, which is worse than a missing label.

rowFilter.kommune_befolkning_alder.alder.name: alder_16_17
rowFilter.kommune_befolkning_alder.alder.description: Residents aged 16-17. Disjoint band, and the one that completes 0_17.

rowFilter.kommune_befolkning_alder.alder.name: alder_18_66
rowFilter.kommune_befolkning_alder.alder.description: Residents aged 18-66 (working age, to the 67 pension threshold). Disjoint band.

rowFilter.kommune_befolkning_alder.alder.name: alder_80_plus
rowFilter.kommune_befolkning_alder.alder.description: Residents aged 80 and over, including SSB's open-ended '105+' bucket. Disjoint band. Built from age_min, not age_int — age_int is NULL for '105+', so banding on it would silently drop those residents.

rowFilter.kommune_befolkning_alder.alder.name: alder_0_17
rowFilter.kommune_befolkning_alder.alder.description:
Residents aged 0-17. ⚠️ A ROLL-UP of 0_5 + 6_15 + 16_17, NOT a
seventh band — adding it to the disjoint bands double-counts.
The child-poverty denominator, so that coverage_gap_barnefattigdom's
share can be read against a population rather than against itself.

rowFilter.kommune_befolkning_alder.alder.name: alder_67_plus
rowFilter.kommune_befolkning_alder.alder.description:
Residents aged 67 and over. ⚠️ A ROLL-UP of 67_79 + 80_plus, NOT a
band. This is the elderly denominator the consumer in #1281 did not
have; 67 is Norway's pension age and the choice of threshold is the
reader's, which is why the two bands are published beside it.

rowFilter.kommune_befolkning_alder.befol.name: befolkning_total
rowFilter.kommune_befolkning_alder.befol.description:
All residents of the kommune in that year. Equals the six disjoint
bands summed.

🔴 Sexes are FILTERED, not summed: SSB's Kjonn dimension codes '0' as
ALL, so summing every sex row would double the population of every
kommune in Norway. The model selects male and female explicitly, and
the singular test bands_sum_to_the_population_total is what would
catch it if that ever stopped being true.

rowFilter.activity_catalog.activity_id.name: activity_id
rowFilter.activity_catalog.activity_id.description:
Composite slug (e.g. 'redcross-besokstjeneste'). Stable across
refreshes. Unique within this view.

rowFilter.activity_catalog.ngo_orgnr.name: ngo_orgnr
rowFilter.activity_catalog.ngo_orgnr.description: 9-digit Brreg organisasjonsnummer of the NGO offering the activity.

rowFilter.activity_catalog.canonical_nam.name: canonical_name
rowFilter.activity_catalog.canonical_nam.description: Atlas's canonical Norwegian name for the activity.

rowFilter.activity_catalog.service_categ.name: service_category_code
rowFilter.activity_catalog.service_categ.description:
ICNPO-derived service category code (e.g. 'health',
'social-services'). FK to ref_atlas_service_category.

rowFilter.activity_catalog.service_categ.name: service_category_label_no
rowFilter.activity_catalog.service_categ.description:
Human-readable Norwegian label for service_category_code,
joined from ref_atlas_service_category.

rowFilter.activity_catalog.is_active.name: is_active
rowFilter.activity_catalog.is_active.description:
Whether this activity is still offered by the NGO. Inactive
activities are kept so historical analysis can still resolve
activity_id values.

rowFilter.activity_catalog.chapter_count.name: chapter_count
rowFilter.activity_catalog.chapter_count.description:
Count of distinct active chapters offering this activity. Zero
when the activity exists in dim_activity but no active chapter
provides it (rare but possible during transitions).

rowFilter.distrikt_summary.chapter_id.name: chapter_id
rowFilter.distrikt_summary.chapter_id.description:
Composite slug for the regional chapter (e.g.
'redcross-oslo'). Stable across refreshes. Unique within this
view.

rowFilter.distrikt_summary.name.name: name
rowFilter.distrikt_summary.name.description: Display name for the regional chapter (e.g. 'Oslo Røde Kors').

rowFilter.distrikt_summary.kommune_nr.name: kommune_nr
rowFilter.distrikt_summary.kommune_nr.description:
4-digit kommune code where the regional chapter is
headquartered. NULL for distrikter without a single HQ
kommune. Note: kommune_coverage_count tells you how many
*child* kommuner the distrikt covers — that's the operational
footprint, not where the office sits.

rowFilter.distrikt_summary.kommune_name.name: kommune_name
rowFilter.distrikt_summary.kommune_name.description: Joined from dim_kommune. NULL when kommune_nr is NULL.

rowFilter.distrikt_summary.ngo_orgnr.name: ngo_orgnr
rowFilter.distrikt_summary.ngo_orgnr.description: 9-digit Brreg organisasjonsnummer of the NGO this distrikt belongs to.

rowFilter.distrikt_summary.child_count.name: child_count
rowFilter.distrikt_summary.child_count.description:
Count of active local chapters whose parent_chapter_id equals
this distrikt's chapter_id. The "lokalforeninger" total shown
in the UI.

rowFilter.distrikt_summary.kommune_cover.name: kommune_coverage_count
rowFilter.distrikt_summary.kommune_cover.description:
Count of distinct kommuner served by this distrikt's active
children (kommune_nr IS NOT NULL). The operational footprint;
may be smaller than child_count when multiple children share
a kommune.

rowFilter.ngo_index.orgnr.name: orgnr
rowFilter.ngo_index.orgnr.description:
9-digit Brreg organisasjonsnummer (text — leading zeros are
preserved). Natural key for this view.

rowFilter.ngo_index.brand_name.name: brand_name
rowFilter.ngo_index.brand_name.description:
Common brand name when distinct from legal name (e.g.
'Sanitetskvinnene' vs N.K.S.). NULL when the brand equals
the legal name.

rowFilter.ngo_index.website_url.name: website_url
rowFilter.ngo_index.website_url.description: NGO's primary website. Used as the outbound link from the index page.

rowFilter.ngo_index.tier.name: tier
rowFilter.ngo_index.tier.description:
Structural-fit tier (A / B / C) from
docs/research/ngo-landscape.md. v1 includes Tier A only.

rowFilter.ngo_index.chapter_data_shape.name: chapter_data_shape
rowFilter.ngo_index.chapter_data_shape.description:
How this NGO's per-chapter activity data is shaped — drives
which ingest pattern it uses. Values: 'api_canonical',
'cms_bins', 'programme_only', 'no_structure'.

rowFilter.ngo_index.has_chapters.name: has_chapters
rowFilter.ngo_index.has_chapters.description:
Whether this NGO DECLARES that it has chapters — an editorial fact
from dim_ngo, recorded when the organisation is curated.

Not the same question as has_supply, which is chapter_count > 0 and
therefore an ingest OUTCOME: does Atlas hold chapter rows for this
organisation yet. They agree today only because all curated NGOs
declare has_chapters true and all have been ingested. The first NGO
curated before its chapters land makes them disagree, and a consumer
filtering on the wrong one loses it without an error.

rowFilter.ngo_index.primary_focus.name: primary_focus
rowFilter.ngo_index.primary_focus.description: One-line description of the NGO's main mission area.

rowFilter.ngo_index.icnpo_code_1.name: icnpo_code_1
rowFilter.ngo_index.icnpo_code_1.description:
ICNPO classification code (primary). See ref_icnpo. NULL when
unclassified.

rowFilter.ngo_index.icnpo_code_2.name: icnpo_code_2
rowFilter.ngo_index.icnpo_code_2.description: ICNPO classification code (secondary). NULL when not used.

rowFilter.ngo_index.icnpo_code_3.name: icnpo_code_3
rowFilter.ngo_index.icnpo_code_3.description: ICNPO classification code (tertiary). NULL when not used.

rowFilter.ngo_index.chapter_count.name: chapter_count
rowFilter.ngo_index.chapter_count.description:
Count of active chapters for this NGO (filtered by
dim_chapter.is_active = true). Zero if the NGO has no chapters
or all chapters are dormant.

🔴 AND A THIRD CASE, WHICH IS THE ONE TRUE TODAY: zero also
means ATLAS HOLDS NO CHAPTER DATA. All eleven organisations
currently report `has_chapters = true` with `chapter_count = 0`,
and a consumer reading the pair gets a contradiction
(urb-agents #1388).

🔵 The two columns answer different questions and both answers
are correct. `has_chapters` is a property of the ORGANISATION —
it is structured in local chapters — and comes from the roster.
`chapter_count` is a property of ATLAS — how many it holds — and
comes from `dim_chapter`, which is empty until the Red Cross
data arrives.

⚠️ So `has_chapters = true, chapter_count = 0` reads "this
organisation has chapters and Atlas has none of them", not "its
chapters are all dormant". See `activity_catalog`,
`distrikt_summary` and `kommune_local_chapters`, which are
empty for the same reason and say so.

🔵 Same shape as the FHI suppression note: the data is right and
the reading is the defect.

rowFilter.ngo_index.has_supply.name: has_supply
rowFilter.ngo_index.has_supply.description:
Convenience boolean: chapter_count > 0. True when the NGO has
at least one active chapter — i.e. it appears on the supply
side of Atlas.

rowFilter.unattributed_totals.relation.name: relation
rowFilter.unattributed_totals.relation.description: The published relation this remainder belongs to, e.g. `kommune_ngo_totals`. Not a foreign key: it names a relation, not a row.

rowFilter.unattributed_totals.measure.name: measure
rowFilter.unattributed_totals.measure.description: The column of that relation the value would have contributed to.

rowFilter.unattributed_totals.reason.name: reason
rowFilter.unattributed_totals.reason.description:
Why the value is unattributable.

`no_kommune_nr` — upstream publishes the record with no
municipality at all. For Brreg this is 10.3 % of active
voluntary units and is what Brreg itself publishes; it is not
an Atlas defect.

`kommune_nr_not_current` — the record HAS a kommune_nr and it
is not one of the current municipalities. 🔴 Today these are
all Svalbard (2100): a real code, absent from SSB's Klass 131,
so `kommune_ngo_totals` emits no row for it. Without this
reason the relation named 7 489 of 7 532 and the obvious
reconciliation came out 43 short with no error anywhere
(urb-agents #1318). Historical kommune codes would land here
too if Brreg ever used one.

`sentinel_9999` — upstream attributes the value to its own
'Uoppgitt' bucket. ⚠️ Note this is the same 9999 that
`classify_region_code` calls `unspecified_national` and that
`dim_kommune.is_active` still returns as a municipality.

rowFilter.unattributed_totals.source_id.name: source_id
rowFilter.unattributed_totals.source_id.description: The upstream source the quantity comes from.

rowFilter.unattributed_totals.year.name: year
rowFilter.unattributed_totals.year.description: Calendar year, where the quantity is time-varying. NULL for register snapshots like Brreg, which have no year dimension — a null here means "not applicable", never "unknown".

rowFilter.unattributed_totals.unattribut.name: unattributed_value
rowFilter.unattributed_totals.unattribut.description: The part that belongs to no municipality. Add this to a sum over the per-kommune relation to reconcile with the upstream national figure.

rowFilter.unattributed_totals.total_valu.name: total_value
rowFilter.unattributed_totals.total_valu.description: The whole quantity, attributed and unattributed together. The denominator for the share.

rowFilter.unattributed_totals.unattribut.name: unattributed_share_pct
rowFilter.unattributed_totals.unattribut.description: `unattributed_value` as a percentage of `total_value`, to one decimal. NULL when total_value is zero, because a share of nothing is undefined rather than zero.

rowFilter.indicator_summary.source_id.name: source_id
rowFilter.indicator_summary.source_id.description:
Atlas source identifier, e.g. 'ssb-08764'. Joins back to
fact_kommune_indicators.source_id and to the source declarations
in indicators/sources.yml.

rowFilter.indicator_summary.contents_cod.name: contents_code
rowFilter.indicator_summary.contents_cod.description:
Source-specific ContentsCode verbatim from upstream (e.g.
'EUskala60', 'Folkemengde'). Combined with source_id forms the
natural key of this view.

rowFilter.indicator_summary.contents_lab.name: contents_label
rowFilter.indicator_summary.contents_lab.description:
Human-readable label for contents_code, verbatim from upstream.
NULL only if every contributing row had a NULL label (rare).

rowFilter.indicator_summary.latest_year.name: latest_year
rowFilter.indicator_summary.latest_year.description:
Most recent calendar year for which this (source_id,
contents_code) has a VALUE in fact_kommune_indicators. The
coverage and value-range columns below are computed against
this year only.

🔴 THIS CHANGED ON 2026-09-21 AND THE OLD BEHAVIOUR WAS WRONG.
It was "has any rows", which pointed at years the publisher had
not released yet: upstream ships the full grid, so a row exists
with a NULL value. Seven of `ssb-06913`'s eight series resolved
to 2026 with `kommuner_with_value` 0 and both value bounds null
— a live series whose summary read as empty (urb-agents #1351).

⚠️ IT IS THE LATEST YEAR AN ACTIVE, NON-SENTINEL KOMMUNE HAS A
VALUE — the same subject the coverage below is counted over. A
first version filtered only on `value is not null` and was
defeated by SSB zero-filling retired kommune codes: 0101 Halden
(-2019) and 0801 Kragerø (-1959) carry a literal 0 for every
year forever, so the year looked populated while every active
kommune was null there. `latest_year` and `kommuners_with_value`
disagreed about which rows count (urb-agents #1354).

⚠️ A series with no value in ANY year keeps the newest year it
has rows for, rather than going null. Disappearing from the
catalogue is the worse failure: "0 of 357" invites a question,
an absent row does not.

⚠️ READ IT WITH `latest_year_window_years`. For a windowed
source this is the FIRST year of the window, not the year of
the data, and rendering it alone prints a date that is wrong by
up to four years.

rowFilter.indicator_summary.kommuner_wit.name: kommuner_with_value
rowFilter.indicator_summary.kommuner_wit.description:
Count of active kommuner (kommune_is_active = true) that have a
non-NULL value for this indicator at latest_year. The headline
coverage number on the data explorer.

rowFilter.indicator_summary.kommuner_wit.name: kommuner_with_null
rowFilter.indicator_summary.kommuner_wit.description:
🔴 FOR AN `fhi-*` SOURCE THIS IS SUPPRESSION, NOT ABSENCE, AND THE
TWO LEAD TO OPPOSITE CONCLUSIONS IN A NEED INDEX.

FHI hides small numbers by policy. Quoted from FHI's own table
metadata (table 377, read 2026-09-22):

  "Statistikk basert på færre enn 6 tilfeller skjules av
   personvernhensyn... Dersom mer enn 20 prosent av tallene i en
   tidsserie er skjult av personvernhensyn, skjules hele
   tidsserien for ikke å skape et skjevt inntrykk av situasjonen
   i kommunen."

So FHI hides a cell under ~6 cases, and hides the WHOLE SERIES
when more than 20% of it is hidden — explicitly to avoid giving a
skewed impression of that kommune. ⚠️ A consumer that reads the
resulting gap as "no need here" is producing exactly the skew the
suppression exists to prevent, and doing it in the direction that
moves help away from the smallest places.

🔵 MEASURED, and the shape is unambiguous (urb-agents #1369,
#1379): 105 kommuner are missing from 10 or more `fhi-*` series,
median population 1,452, monotonic in population. `1151 Utsira`,
219 people, is missing from 15. EVERY kommune is absent from at
least three series — so a kommune appearing here is ordinary and
is not a defect to report.

⚠️ The thresholds above are table 377's; the policy is FHI-wide
but each table states its own. Read the source's metadata rather
than assuming 6.

🔵 It is NOT suppression for SSB sources. SSB zero-fills instead —
a dissolved kommune carries a literal 0 forever — which is a
different failure and was the cause of the `latest_year` defect
fixed in a657f4f. Two publishers, two conventions, and the same
column has to be read differently for each.

Count of active kommuner that have a row at latest_year but
value IS NULL (i.e. upstream suppressed the cell). Inactive
kommuner are not counted.

rowFilter.indicator_summary.min_value.name: min_value
rowFilter.indicator_summary.min_value.description:
Minimum non-NULL value across all rows at latest_year, regardless
of whether the kommune is active. NULL if no row had a value.

rowFilter.indicator_summary.max_value.name: max_value
rowFilter.indicator_summary.max_value.description:
Maximum non-NULL value across all rows at latest_year, regardless
of whether the kommune is active. NULL if no row had a value.

rowFilter.indicator_summary.upstream_upd.name: upstream_updated
rowFilter.indicator_summary.upstream_upd.description:
Most recent fact_kommune_indicators.updated_at across the rows
that contributed to this summary. Useful for staleness checks
per indicator without joining to raw.*.

rowFilter.indicator_summary.upstream_tit.name: upstream_title
rowFilter.indicator_summary.upstream_tit.description:
What this series is ABOUT, from the source catalogue. The
subject was previously unreachable from this view — a
consumer used 8 of 195 series and missed the ones matching
its own question, because `contents_label` describes the
UNIT ("Andel (prosent)") and the subject lived only in an
opaque slug (urb-agents #1250, #1252). Joined from
mart_meta_sources; NULL only if a source is absent from the
catalogue, which `relationships` below asserts cannot happen.

rowFilter.indicator_summary.publisher.name: publisher
rowFilter.indicator_summary.publisher.description:
Who publishes the upstream series (SSB, FHI, Bufdir, Brreg).
Joined from mart_meta_sources.

rowFilter.indicator_summary.eu_theme.name: eu_theme
rowFilter.indicator_summary.eu_theme.description:
EU high-value-dataset theme. Populated for all 44 sources —
filter on it to ask "what does Atlas have about X?", which is
the question this view could not previously answer.

rowFilter.indicator_summary.tags.name: tags
rowFilter.indicator_summary.tags.description:
Topic vocabulary from the source manifest, e.g.
['provider:brreg', 'topic:ngo-supply']. Joined from
mart_meta_sources.

🔴 QUOTE THE VALUE. A tag contains a colon, and unquoted it is
rejected: `?tags=cs.{topic:ngo-supply}` returns 22P02 malformed
array literal. The working form is
`?tags=cs.{"topic:ngo-supply"}`.

⚠️ The unquoted spelling was published HERE, in this description,
until 2026-09-20 — so a consumer following the documentation got
an error and had to work the quoting out for itself (urb-agents
#1281). Same class as the `personer` description: the contract
said something a consumer acted on and it was wrong.

rowFilter.indicator_summary.latest_year_.name: latest_year_window_years
rowFilter.indicator_summary.latest_year_.description:
How many calendar years `latest_year` covers: 1 for an annual
series, 5 for `fhi-selvmord`, 3 for `fhi-mobbing`. The span is
`latest_year` to `latest_year + latest_year_window_years - 1`.

🔴 WHY IT IS A COLUMN AND NOT A SENTENCE. The window was already
stated in prose in this catalogue. On 2026-09-21 it was misread
twice in one day in opposite directions — a reviewer called a
live `fhi-selvmord` series six years stale, and a consumer
shipped the caption «Mobbetallene er fra 2022» for a 2022-2024
window. The consumer's proposed workaround, matching `/1-year/i`
against the description, false-positives on `fhi-kpr-1aar`,
whose title contains "KPR 1-year" and which is annual anyway
(urb-agents #1331).

🔵 CROSS-CHECK IT AGAINST `meta_dimensions`, WHICH SAID ALL THIS
FIRST. `?code=in.(AAR,Tid)&select=source_id,meaning,value_format`
carries the upstream's own description of its time dimension. On
2026-09-21 a consumer, ops-dev and this agent each derived the
windowing independently while that relation was already published
and already said it — and the claim "exactly two FHI sources are
windowed", used as evidence, was wrong; the catalogue named three
(urb-agents #1333).

⚠️ IT IS A `max()` OVER THE KOMMUNER AT `latest_year`, because
this view's grain is one row per (source, contents_code) and the
window lives on the fact row. That is only honest if the window
is uniform across kommuner within an indicator-year, which is
asserted by the singular test
`window_is_uniform_within_an_indicator_year`. If that test ever
fails, this column is lossy and the failure is the warning.

rowFilter.meta_sources.source_id.name: source_id
rowFilter.meta_sources.source_id.description: Atlas catalogue id; primary key. Matches `_sources_manifest.source_id`.

rowFilter.meta_sources.upstream_id.name: upstream_id
rowFilter.meta_sources.upstream_id.description: Upstream's own identifier (SSB table number, FHI dataset slug, etc.).

rowFilter.meta_sources.upstream_url.name: upstream_url
rowFilter.meta_sources.upstream_url.description: Canonical link to the data on the upstream's site (often the API endpoint).

rowFilter.meta_sources.upstream_landing_.name: upstream_landing_page
rowFilter.meta_sources.upstream_landing_.description:
Human-browsable web page describing the dataset (DCAT-AP `dcat:landingPage`).
Empty when `upstream_url` is already browsable; clients fall back to that.

rowFilter.meta_sources.upstream_title.name: upstream_title
rowFilter.meta_sources.upstream_title.description: Source's authoritative title at the upstream (usually Norwegian).

rowFilter.meta_sources.description.name: description
rowFilter.meta_sources.description.description: One-paragraph framing for the customer-facing catalogue.

rowFilter.meta_sources.periodicity.name: periodicity
rowFilter.meta_sources.periodicity.description:
Update cadence as ISO 8601 (`P1Y` / `P3M` / `P1M` / `P1D`)
or `irregular`. More precise than the `cadence:` tag.

rowFilter.meta_sources.eu_theme.name: eu_theme
rowFilter.meta_sources.eu_theme.description:
EU Publications Office Data Theme code (one of 13: `AGRI`, `ECON`,
`EDUC`, `ENER`, `ENVI`, `GOVE`, `HEAL`, `INTR`, `JUST`, `REGI`,
`SOCI`, `TECH`, `TRAN`). Aligns with Felles datakatalog / DCAT-AP.

rowFilter.meta_sources.attribution.name: attribution
rowFilter.meta_sources.attribution.description:
Citation string for academic / legal compliance (e.g.
"Kilde: Statistisk sentralbyrå, tabell 08764").

rowFilter.meta_sources.tags.name: tags
rowFilter.meta_sources.tags.description:
`text[]` of namespaced tags: `provider:<X>`, `topic:<X>`,
`geo:<X>`, `cadence:<X>`, `eu_theme:<X>`. Filter via PostgREST's
array-contains operator, QUOTING the value because it contains a
colon: `?tags=cs.{"topic:ngo-supply"}`. Unquoted it returns 22P02
malformed array literal. Always 5 entries (one per declared
namespace).

rowFilter.meta_sources.last_ingested_at.name: last_ingested_at
rowFilter.meta_sources.last_ingested_at.description:
`MAX(finished_at)` from `raw.ingest_runs` filtered to
successful runs (`exit_code = 0`). NULL until the source has
at least one successful run on the current cluster.

rowFilter.meta_sources.last_upstream_upd.name: last_upstream_update_at
rowFilter.meta_sources.last_upstream_upd.description:
`MAX(upstream_updated_at)` from successful ingest runs.
NULL when the source hasn't run yet OR its ingest module
doesn't capture the upstream's "updated" field (Red Cross
web scrape, Brreg per-entity fetch).

rowFilter.meta_sources.latest_row_count.name: latest_row_count
rowFilter.meta_sources.latest_row_count.description:
`rows_parsed` from the most recent successful run. NULL when
the source has zero successful runs on the current cluster.

rowFilter.meta_sources.total_runs.name: total_runs
rowFilter.meta_sources.total_runs.description:
Count of successful runs ever recorded for this source. 0 when
no successful run exists.

rowFilter.meta_sources.downstream_model_.name: downstream_model_count
rowFilter.meta_sources.downstream_model_.description:
Number of distinct downstream dbt models that derive from this
source via the `lineage` seed. 0 for sources not yet wired
into a mart.

🔴 DO NOT READ THIS AS "IS IT SERVED". It counts models, and a
model is not a consumer surface. A source feeding 357 rows into
a published relation and a source whose only model reaches
nothing both report a positive count. Use `served_as`.

⚠️ On 2026-09-21 this field produced a statement to a consumer
that "the eight FHI sources" were served, when it was seven —
`fhi-innvandrere` has one model, 32,720 rows and no published
series. Four parties had each built a different partial proxy
for the question this field looks like it answers, and three
were wrong the same day (urb-agents #1344).

🔴 AND THIS NUMBER CAN CHANGE FOR TWO REASONS THAT LOOK
IDENTICAL. Either a model genuinely shipped, or the lineage it
is computed from was CORRECTED. A consumer reading it twice
cannot tell an honest value change from an accuracy fix: on
2026-09-21 the demo consumer read it morning and evening, got
9 and 1, and had no way to know which it was seeing
(urb-agents #1348).

🔵 `lineage` is generated from the dbt manifest and committed,
so it can be stale — 103 edges were missing that day, some for
weeks. `check-lineage-is-current.sh` now fails CI on drift, so
the accuracy kind of change should stop happening. It cannot
be detected retroactively in a value you already read.

rowFilter.meta_sources.served_as.name: served_as
rowFilter.meta_sources.served_as.description:
The `api_v1` relations a consumer can actually reach this source
through, as a Postgres `text[]`. **Empty means nothing published
depends on it** — that is the gap, and it is the one question
`downstream_model_count` cannot answer.

Filter for the gap with `?served_as=eq.{}`, or for a specific
surface with `?served_as=cs.{indicator_summary}`.

🔵 NOT A PLAIN LINEAGE JOIN, DELIBERATELY. A relation derived
from `fact_kommune_indicators` is only claimed when the source
actually has rows in that fact.

The case that forced that design: `ssb-06913` fed the fact and
so reached four published relations on paper while contributing
ZERO rows to them — its `kommune_nr` regex never matched, so
783,104 rows were discarded downstream. A structural boolean
would have called it served and become the fifth wrong proxy.
It was fixed the same day (urb-agents #1345) and now reports
those four relations, which is the column working rather than
the example expiring.

⚠️ THE CATALOGUE RELATIONS ARE EXCLUDED. `meta_sources`,
`meta_endpoints` and `meta_dimensions` hold a row for every
source by construction, so naming them would be the same value
on every row. They describe a source; they do not serve it.

🔴 IT DOES NOT ASSERT THAT ANY NAMED RELATION CONTAINS ROWS.
For a relation derived from the fact, the source is checked to
have rows there. For every other relation the claim is
LINEAGE ONLY — what the source WOULD serve if it had data.

⚠️ THE CASE THAT PROVES IT: `redcross-branches` has
`total_runs` 0 and has never ingested, and it still lists five
relations, three of which hold zero rows. A source that has
never run looks served.

🔵 THE COMPANION CHECK IS ON THIS SAME ROW. Read `served_as`
with `total_runs` and `latest_row_count`: lineage says what
could arrive, those say whether anything did.

⚠️ AN EARLIER VERSION OF THIS PARAGRAPH SAID THE SAME THING AND
DID NOT WORK. It read "for non-fact relations this is
reachability, not volume", naming `brreg_enhet` and
`dim_kommune` — relations that are never empty, so the warning
was abstract. ops-dev read it and built a gate on the field
within the hour (urb-agents #1346). A caveat that names no
failing case is a caveat nobody applies.

🔵 Excluding never-ingested sources outright was considered and
rejected: it would collapse "has never run" into "is not
modelled", losing the distinction between `redcross-branches`
(five relations waiting for data) and the sources deferred in
BACKLOG (no relation at all). Say the word if that trade is
wrong.

🔵 Derived from the same artefact the CI gate reads, so the two
cannot drift: `check-every-source-is-served.sh` and this column
both resolve the source against the generated `api_v1` relation
list.

⚠️ THE GATE AND THIS COLUMN CAN DISAGREE, AND THAT IS CORRECT.
The gate is static and cannot see a source that is wired up and
delivers nothing, so it will report fewer gaps than this column
does. The gate answers "is it wired"; this answers "does it
arrive". Neither count is written here on purpose — a number in
a published description goes stale silently, which is most of
why this column had to be written at all.

rowFilter.indicator_missing_kommuner.kom.name: kommune_nr
rowFilter.indicator_missing_kommuner.kom.description:
4-digit zero-padded kommune code. FK to dim_kommune; only
active kommuner with no value at latest_year are listed.
